title.narrative: Ho Chi Minh City Bicycle Initiative

description.narrative: In Ho Chi Minh City, while motorcycle remains the most popular means of transportation, the Department of Transport launched the first public bicycle service in Ho Chi Minh City in December 2021. The implementation of the public bicycle model will not only diversify urban transport modes in the city centre but also create favourable health benefits for users. Moreover, it is more affordable, reduces traffic and air pollution and creates new tourism products, contributing to the economic recovery and development of the city. In this context, the Netherlands Consulate-general (CG) in Ho Chi Minh City will stimulate the process of strengthening the local government knowledge in cycling and also explore the opportunities for collaboration and cooperation between the Netherlands and Ho Chi Minh City. This could be made possible by knowledge exchange from the Dutch cities that have been through similar developments.The Netherlands Consulate General plays a facilitating role to initiate potential connections with relevant local and international partners. More importantly, promoting cycling in HCMC aligns with the broader goals of the Embassy and CG to promote the United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals (SDG).SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities. Promoting sustainable forms of transportation also supportsSDG 3: Good Health and Wellbeing,SDG 10: Reduced InequalitySDG 13: Climate Action andSDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals.

title.narrative: Number of identified opportunities for investment and/or follow-up PSD projects - Total

comment.narrative: A) Investment in bicycle parking facilities (1): the current bicycle parking facilities in HCMC are built by Tri Nam Group. In the future, when cycling being scaled up along with the new metro line, there will be a need to invest in bicycle parking facilities which shall be implemented by the local authority b) Knowledge and experience in bicycle infrastructure planning: There is a need for knowledge and experience on urban planning, specifically for bicycle infrastructure, to develop a bicycle strategy and future urban plans. c) Production and sales of bikes and bike infrastructure related products: The ownership of bikes has decreased over the years. With a stimulation of active mobility and bike infrastructure the demand of private bicycles will rise. This could offer future business for Dutch bike (related) producers. d) Tourism: Vietnam is a popular location for tourists and there is lots of potential to improve sustainable tourism. e) Data: Currently, there is almost no data available about the number of cyclists in Vietnam. When there is data available, the case for more infrastructure and campaigns can be justified.
